post_review_additions.provenance: Added AFTER an independent review of the first run, which reproduced the primary numbers and raised: (1) race stints and practice runs start on different set states (82% of practice race-sim runs start at tyre age >= 6, race stints mostly at 2-5); (2) the gradient test is underpowered, so 'not supported' is not a null; (3) the pre-stated placebo was vacuous; (4) the cross-sectional race estimator is not identified. These specifications were NOT in the original pre-registration. They were fixed in the module docstring before being run and were not tuned on their output. One deviation: the strict matched level gap (>= 3 runs per cell and context) leaves very few cells, so the headline level gap is the pooled-lap version at >= 1 run per cell, reported beside the strict one.

twfe_gradient.design: per event-season: lap time ~ run effect + lap effect (race) / 10-minute session-bin effect (practice) + tyre age with a compound-specific slope, one compound pair at a time; contrast = slope(a) - slope(b); DiD = race contrast - practice contrast; RE-weighted mean over events; >= 2 runs per compound and context; window 6-16; sign-flip permutation = compound labels permuted within event. Fuel, track evolution and temperature are common to compounds and cancel.

uniform_damping.note: a uniform damping factor alone produces a negative additive beta because softer tyres have larger practice slopes

power_additive_trend.note: MDE = smallest |beta| (s/lap per softness step) with >= 80% power under the observed design; SOFT-HARD is twice that. The observed beta is below the MDE, so 'not supported' there is underpowered, not a null.

referee_additions.provenance: Added after referee findings on the drafted paper, and after the post-review additions. Not pre-registered; computed with fixed seeds and not tuned on output. Contents: (1) what the start-age matching actually selects and designs matched on the feed's FreshTyre flag; (2) a scripted reconciliation of the race-only compound trend across estimators; (3) the placebo-adjusted gap; (4) Holm adjustment over the three TWFE pair tests; (5) the lead estimand.

set_state_counts.definition: start_age = TyreLife of the first retained lap of the run (pit laps, non-green laps, laps > 1.10x the driver's best and stint outliers removed); runs are consecutive-lap blocks, so a gap splits a stint. fresh = the feed's FreshTyre flag for the stint (one value per stint). stint_start_age = TyreLife at the stint's first timed lap.

twfe_primary_holm.note: Holm step-down over the three pairwise permutation tests; permutation p cannot go below 1/(P+1).

referee_additions.lead_estimand_definition: gap = pooled race slope minus pooled practice slope (s/lap, same within-run estimator, window 6-16, events with both contexts); ratio = race slope / practice slope; 95% intervals are event-season cluster bootstraps. The gap is the lead estimand; the ratio is secondary and unstable for HARD.

differences_between_the_two_analyses: estimator: within-run / TWFE contrast (car versus itself) versus a design demeaned by (event, lap) across cars
window: tyre ages 6-16 versus all ages
run set: events with both contexts (Table 3) versus every event with the compounds
unit: label rank (HARD/MEDIUM/SOFT) versus C-number step in the mixed model
explanation.one_sentence: The sign of the race-only compound trend depends on how the slope is identified, not on the data: within-run and two-way fixed-effects contrasts, which compare a car with itself, put it near zero (+0.009 s/lap per step softer, 95% CI -0.003 to +0.021, all seasons; -0.002 in 2026), whereas designs that compare cars with each other at the same lap, such as the mixed model's -0.0114 in 2026, give negative trends on identical cells (-0.026 for the field-demeaned slope and -0.044 for the compound-demeaned one, all seasons); the positive race-side TWFE contrasts in Table 3 are means over only the events that also have practice, and over all events they are +0.009 (SOFT-HARD), +0.013 (MEDIUM-HARD) and -0.031 (SOFT-MEDIUM), i.e. neither uniform nor additive.
